summary_md:
**Espetero ([@espetero_dev](https://x.com/espetero_dev/status/2115172061085876412))** releases **Espetero 0.1.2**, a C++20 + Metal LLM inference server for Apple silicon (no Python) that loads MLX and GGUF files and exposes OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama APIs so Claude Code works against it. The self-reply thread adds benchmarks and design notes:

- One GPU pass per step for everything in flight (prompts, replies, images, draft verification).
- Qwen3.8-27B 4-bit on an M4 Max: 59 tok/s single-user with the model's MTP head, 161 tok/s total with 8 users; on the same GGUF as llama.cpp it reports 47 vs 33 tok/s.
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B MoE, 6B active): 79 tok/s with MTP on a 128 GB Mac Studio; DeepSeek V4.1-Flash (552B) experimentally at ~10 tok/s on one 128 GB Mac by streaming cold experts from SSD.
- Lossless by default, JSON Schema compiled to token masks, tool calls, vision and on-disk prompt checkpoints.

referenced_urls.title: GitHub - JarJarFran/espetero: Fast LLM inference for Apple silicon: a native Metal engine with OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama APIs

relevance: A new local serving engine with batched multi-agent throughput numbers on the ~27B and Flash-Next tiers.
